chapter: New York dance bands and Dorsey
title: Roger Wolfe Kahn's band and the cost of being a millionaire's son
summary: Freeman plays six months with Roger Wolfe Kahn's studio-player band, losing jobs when owners try to sell clubs to Otto Kahn's son.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And I think the first one was with Roger Wolfe Kahn. Now, as you know, Roger Wolfe Kahn's father was the famous financier, Otto Kahn, and every time we got a job the owners of the club found that Roger was the

son of one of the richest men in the world, Otto Kahn, so they would try to get Roger to buy the nightclub or restaurant which Roger refused to do, so that would be the end of our job and I said that being this wealthy was an obstacle in the way of getting work, because I was only with him about six months and we had about three jobs in the six months.

And it was a marvelous band and all the best arrangers in the field were to go on and become composers out in Hollywood and it was beautiful music to play, Of course, it was dance music, and I was just a jazz soloist in the band, and Roger was a marvelous guy to work for.
It was sort of like Isham Jones.

Well, it was better -- if I may say, the musicians were the top players, session players in New York, and they would be sending in substitutes like Manny Klein and all the great -- who I just saw recently in Holland. He was a super session man, as you know.
Anyway, that went on for about six months because we couldn't keep a job once they knew Roger was so wealthy and business wasn't good, why you know, buy in or get out.
